claims.proposition_evaluated: On August 26, 2026, Infrastructure Committee rejected administration’s recommended hold on the remaining programme routes rather than adopting it, and City Council had not adopted that hold by September 25, 2026.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged. Item 1.4 added both replacement versions of Attachment 5, and item 7.6 lists all three; the minutes do not identify an operative version. Under the brief’s rule, Version 2 is primary. It calls for evaluation and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction, but does not expressly say construction or advancement of the 14 listed routes waits for either step. The original expressly removes them from programme scope for 2026 and 2027. Version 1 conditionally removes routes affecting travel lanes or parking, without establishing that all 14 listed routes meet that condition. At item 7.6, Rutherford’s amendment to delete accelerated-construction wording failed 2–2: Rutherford and Clarke in favour, Salvador and Janz opposed. Salvador’s motion to continue the previously approved scope, advance tender-ready routes and prepare for 2027 construction failed 2–2: Salvador and Janz in favour, Rutherford and Clarke opposed. No motion to adopt Recommendation 1 was put. Rutherford’s motion to keep Attachment 4 private carried 4–0; procedural motions to meet in private and return to public carried 5–0 each. The committee therefore left Recommendation 1 without a substantive decision. The six committee members were Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz, Mayor Knack and Paquette; only the first four voted on the amendment and main motion. Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright attended as non-members. The carried September 2 Executive Committee items show a related funding motion was not made and was renewed as a notice. The September 8 City Council item 11.6 laid that notice over to October 6; it did not decide Recommendation 1. No Council adoption or override is documented by the as-of date. The prior approved programme scope and Council’s July 7, 2026 decision on the separate 50 Street route remained recorded Council directions. Administration’s route-status statements are not Council decisions. Under the required alternative reading in which non-adoption alone means 'did not support,' the result is Supported. For full City Council as the alternative body, the result is Not established: no consideration of Recommendation 1 is documented in the available records.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Report IS03688 recommended an approach expressly deferring construction or advancement of 14 named, unbuilt programme routes until a further evaluation, report or decision.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged. Recommendation 1 seeks approval of Attachment 5’s approach and says Council approval is required; the report says approval would require no change to CM-20-0330 or its borrowing bylaws. The agenda and minutes list three Attachment 5 versions without selecting one, so Version 2 is the declared primary. Each version lists 13 entries to continue: 50 Street (109A Avenue to Goldbar Park Road); 84 Avenue (Mill Creek Ravine to 91 Street); 100 Street (76 Avenue to 80 Avenue); 107 Avenue (east of Groat Road to 163 Street); 110 Avenue/90 Street and 112 Avenue; 111 Avenue (120 to 121 Street); 114 Avenue (81 to 89 Street); 127 Avenue (97 to 102A Street); 163 Street (87 to 95 Avenue); 163 Street (Stony Plain Road to 107 Avenue); 167/169 Street (Whitemud Drive to 87 Avenue); Kingsway (113 to 122 Street); and Victoria Park Road (116 Street to River Valley Road). Each separately lists 14 entries: 50 Street (101 to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); and Grovenor’s 148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street segments. These are counts by named entry, as the brief requires; splitting the three combined entries yields 18 segments by my calculation. The original expressly removes the 14 entries from programme scope for 2026 and 2027, meeting both deferral readings and yielding Supported for that version. Version 1 retains conditional removal rules for routes affecting travel lanes or parking, but its list does not establish that every named entry is removed; its primary and stricter classifications are Partially supported. Version 2 says remaining routes will be evaluated, with a Q1 2027 report for Council direction and approval, and says the 14 projects may be re-evaluated if Council approves. Neither passage expressly makes their construction or advancement wait; its primary and stricter classifications are Partially supported. The result is version-sensitive. Attachment 3 reports statuses as of August 10: 84 Avenue, 92A Avenue and a combined 93 Street/84 Avenue description were tendered but not started; six entries were originally scheduled for 2026 but no longer viable for installation that year; 50 Street’s southern segment, 95 Avenue, 101 Avenue, 106 Avenue and Grovenor had no delivery schedule, with the 50 Street segment specifically paused for reconsideration. None of the 14 was reported under construction or complete at the primary date. Attachment 3 describes the combined 93 Street/84 Avenue entry differently from Attachment 5, so that match is an identified judgment. I found no dated City record establishing each route’s status specifically on August 26; the alternative-date statuses are unresolved, with no established route change.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between November 30, 2022 and September 25, 2026, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought two City Council motions that each would have left $45 million to $55 million in CM-20-0330, directed the released funds to a named destination and were defeated.
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged. In the November 2023 budget meeting, Principe moved and Rice seconded Capital Budget Amendment 2. Its initial text proposed a $50 million decrease 'towards the tax levy'; the text actually put proposed a $50 million CM-20-0330 reduction with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt. Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Paquette, Sohi, Salvador, Tang, Rutherford, Stevenson and Wright opposed; it failed 4–8. On the $100 million approved base, the reviewer’s calculation is $100 million − $50 million = $50 million, a 50% cut. In December 2024, Principe moved and Rice seconded another Capital Budget Amendment 2, reducing 2025 and 2026 by $33.65 million each. Cartmell, Rice, Rutherford and Principe voted in favour; Knack, Sohi, Salvador, Janz, Tang, Stevenson and Wright opposed; it failed 4–7. The reviewer’s calculation is $33.65 million + $33.65 million = $67.3 million cut, leaving $32.7 million on a $100 million base, outside the primary $45 million–$55 million band but meeting the alternative cut-of-at-least-half rule. Both motions satisfy the primary 'brought' rule and the co-sponsorship alternative because Principe moved and Rice seconded them on separate occasions. The 2023 motion expressly reduces tax-supported debt, a named borrowing destination. The 2024 motion says 'with funding from tax-supported debt,' which identifies the funding source but does not expressly direct released funds elsewhere. Neither names another capital priority. A 2023 Rice/Principe amendment reducing the 2024 capital budget by $26.808 million was withdrawn and does not expressly name this profile; it is not a third defeat. Principe seconded Cartmell’s September 2025 route-suspension motion, which lost 4–9, but it was not a budget-reduction motion. The 2022 approval was $100 million. A City capital update for the period ending September 30, 2024 reports CM-20-0330’s current approved budget as 100,000 in a table labelled $000s, meaning $100 million; this is closer to the 2024 vote than the 2026 report, but does not alone exclude an adjustment between September 30 and the vote. The 2024 remainder is therefore conditional on that base. The partial verdict rests independently on the two documented, defeated reduction motions. Under the alternative amount band both clear half the $100 million base, but the 2024 motion lacks an express named destination, so the alternative classification remains Partially supported. The result is unchanged under the co-sponsorship reading.
